sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate pale to deep reddish brown, the wings white as glass; distance between ocellus and compound eye greater than the ocellus diameter; several veins run from below and outside the subcosta toward the wing apex; pronotum as wide as the head (including the eyes), semicircular, the anterior corners very slightly projecting; media and submedia of the fore wing not united at the wing base but arising separately from the wing scale — the latter character is the main basis both for the name of the species and for distinguishing it from its relatives.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate: body pale reddish brown or deep reddish brown; wings white, transparent as glass; distance between ocellus and compound eye greater than the ocellus diameter; several veins run from below and outside the subcosta to the wing apex; pronotum as wide as the head (including the eyes), semicircular, the anterior corners slightly projecting; media and submedia of the fore wing not united at the true base of the wing but arising separately from the wing scale. Measurements: body length with wings 43 mm; wingspan 76 mm; wing length 35 mm, width 9 mm; body (including head) length 21 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen: total length 72 mm. Localities: Congo (18 June 1893 (month 6), collected by H. Freyschmidt, specimen in the Hamburg Museum; Umangi, collected by E. Wilverth, specimens in the Brussels and Stockholm museums).

note: Adapted from the original description by Sjöstedt 1899 (in German), where the species was named Termes vitrialatus n. sp.; it includes the alate and the queen; "vitrialatus" means "glass-winged". The original measurements use a comma as the decimal point. Type locality Congo; described in the same paper as Termes amplus and T. speciosus.
